title: bovespa Rises on Energy and Mining Gains
body: The Ibovespa advanced 0.5% on Thursday, closing at 187,197 points, driven by gains in energy and mining shares. Petrobras climbed 1.3%, tracking the rally in oil prices after reports that the United States is sending a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East. Vale added 0.6% in a session marked by the absence of iron ore trading in China due to the Golden Week holiday. The major banks ended mixed against a backdrop of elevated global bond yields and renewed inflation concerns fueled by higher energy prices. Banco do Brasil slipped 0.2%, while Bradesco edged up 0.3%. Itaú and Santander retreated 0.3% and 3%, respectively. Retail names outperformed. Magazine Luiza extended the previous session's gains, rising 1.5%. Azzas surged 7% following new proposals related to Farm. On the political front, Datafolha is scheduled to release a new electoral poll after the close of trading. Later in the evening, Globo will host a presidential debate, marking the formal end of the campaign. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has confirmed his participation, while President Lula is unlikely to attend. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: U.S. Bank Reserve Balances Edge Down to $2.88 Trillion, Signaling Gradual Liquidity Pullback
body: Reserve balances held by depository institutions at Federal Reserve Banks in the United States have declined, slipping from $2.969 trillion to $2.881 trillion, according to data updated on 01 October 2026. The roughly $88 billion decrease suggests a modest withdrawal of liquidity from the banking system, as reflected in the lower level of reserves parked at the Fed. While no further contextual data were provided, shifts of this scale are closely watched by market participants as a gauge of banking-sector liquidity conditions and the broader stance of monetary operations. Investors and analysts will be monitoring whether this move marks the beginning of a prolonged trend or a short-term adjustment in reserve levels, with potential implications for short-term funding markets and overall financial conditions in the U.S. banking system. title: Fed Trims Balance Sheet by $5 Billion as Runoff Continues
body: The U.S. Federal Reserve's balance sheet edged down to $6,743 billion, from a previous level of $6,748 billion, according to data updated on 1 October 2026. The $5 billion decline underscores the central bank's ongoing effort to gradually reduce the size of its holdings after years of balance sheet expansion. While the move is modest in scale, the continued runoff reflects the Fed's commitment to normalizing its financial footprint, a process closely watched by markets for its potential impact on liquidity conditions and financial asset pricing. With the balance sheet still elevated by historical standards, even small week-to-week shifts can influence investors' expectations about the future path of monetary policy and longer-term interest rates. Market participants are likely to monitor upcoming releases for signs of whether this gradual pace of reduction will persist or if the Fed will adjust its approach in response to evolving economic data and financial conditions. title: TSX Falls on Losses in Banking and Mining
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index slipped 0.2% to finish at 35,155 on Thursday, dragged down by weakness in mining and banking shares amid persistently elevated global bond yields. Canada's 10-year government bond yield hovered near multi-year highs, even after easing from recent peaks. Financials weighed on the benchmark, with major banks closing lower: Royal Bank of Canada declined 0.7% and Bank of Montreal lost 0.6%. The mining sector also retreated despite firmer gold prices, as higher U.S. Treasury yields and a stronger U.S. dollar pressured the outlook for the group. Agnico Eagle slipped 1.5%, Barrick Gold fell 1.6%, and Franco-Nevada dropped 0.9%. First Quantum Minerals was a notable outlier, rebounding 0.5% after tumbling 15.3% in the previous session. The recovery followed a recommendation by a Panamanian government commission to pursue formal negotiations on a new framework for the Cobre Panamá mine, after authorities had earlier called for the mine's orderly closure. In contrast, energy producers advanced as the recent oil price rally gathered momentum. Canadian Natural Resources climbed 1.7%, while Suncor Energy added 1.8%. Technology stocks also finished higher, mirroring gains in the U.S. tech sector on Wall Street. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: US Stocks Rise as Treasury Selloff Pauses
body: US stocks finished mostly higher on Thursday, reversing earlier declines as the recent selloff in Treasuries paused. The S&P 500 added 0.2%, the Nasdaq rose 0.3%, while the Dow ended little changed. The break in the bond rout pulled 10-year Treasury yields down from their highest level since 2002, with the unwinding of crowded trades helping to drive the rebound. Treasuries also strengthened after Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said more time may be needed to determine whether additional interest-rate hikes are warranted. The stabilization in yields provided some support to credit-sensitive equities. Chipmakers, which have been contending with record levels of debt issuance, mostly advanced. Nvidia gained 1.1%, AMD rose 0.6%, and Micron climbed 3% after issuing an upbeat current-quarter outlook on the back of strong fiscal fourth-quarter results. Before Thursday's move, Treasury yields had extended a months-long climb, driven in part by higher oil prices, which stoked inflation worries and reinforced expectations of further rate increases by major central banks. title: Oil Rises as US Deploys More Forces to Middle East
body: Crude oil prices climbed above $93 per barrel on Thursday following reports that the United States is dispatching a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East. Additional Marine Corps vessels and up to 10,000 more troops are also said to be en route, with the reinforcements expected to arrive by the end of November. The buildup is being interpreted as a potential precursor to expanded US military action against Iran. President Donald Trump has reportedly told aides he anticipates resuming airstrikes on Iran after the November midterm elections. Oil prices are rising even though crude shipments from the Middle East have largely returned to prewar volumes. That recovery, however, remains tenuous. At least three tankers were attacked this week while passing through the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran and its Houthi allies have targeted refineries across the region. Elsewhere, Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have led Moscow to impose a ban on diesel exports. At the same time, Chinese refiners have canceled some gasoline and jet fuel export cargoes that had been scheduled for October. title: Uruguay Trade Balance Swings to Deficit in August
body: Uruguay's trade balance shifted to a deficit of $42.8 million in August 2026, compared with a surplus of $322.49 million in the same month a year earlier. Imports jumped 24.3% year-on-year to $1.06 billion, driven primarily by a 42.2% surge in intermediate goods, underpinned by a 558% spike in oil and distillate purchases. Consumer goods imports grew 17.1%, as imports of autos and other transport equipment climbed 47.2%. By contrast, imports of capital goods fell 11.3%. On the export side, total overseas sales declined 13.4% to $1.02 billion, as exports of primary goods plunged 37.3%, with agriculture and livestock products dropping 40.6%. Offsetting this weakness to some extent, manufacturing exports edged up 1.6%, while exports of utilities expanded 56.6%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Italian Car Registrations Accelerate to 9.9% YoY in September 2026
body: Italy's car market showed strong momentum in September 2026, with new car registrations rising 9.9% year-over-year, according to data updated on 1 October 2026. The gain marks a sharp pickup from August 2026, when registrations were up 3.2% compared with the same month a year earlier. The figures, based on a year-over-year comparison, indicate that September's performance significantly outpaced the previous month's growth. While August reflected a modest improvement versus August of the prior year, September's nearly double‑digit expansion suggests a notable strengthening in demand for new vehicles across the Italian market. The data underscore a clear acceleration in Italy's automotive sector as the third quarter closes, with September's jump highlighting a more robust backdrop than seen earlier in the period.
